input.reasoning_summary:
All three challenges have been refuted by the evidence:

H1 (Full-year rate increase): E14 shows the effective tax rate for full year 2025 was 30% compared to 12% in 2024, confirming a substantial increase for the full year, not just Q3. This refutes the challenge that the increase was only temporary or limited to Q3.

H2 (Other significant factors): While E10, E11, and E12 list various factors that affect the effective tax rate (share-based compensation, R&D credits, foreign-derived intangible income deduction), E1 and E4 explicitly state the rate increase was "mostly due to" OBBBA implementation. E12 shows that for 2024, share-based compensation reduced the rate by 3.7 percentage points, R&D credits by 2.9 points, and FDII by 4.9 points - these are beneficial items that reduce the rate, not factors that would increase it. The evidence confirms OBBBA was indeed the main driver.

H3 (Discrete item exclusion): While E13 does refer to the charge as a "discrete charge," this does not mean it was excluded from the effective tax rate. E1 confirms "Our provision for income taxes in 2025 increased $17.17 billion or 207% compared to 2024, primarily due to an increase in the effective tax rate," and the filing explicitly attributes the effective tax rate increase to OBBBA. The term "discrete" in tax accounting refers to items recorded in a specific quarter rather than spread throughout the year, but they are still included in the effective tax rate calculation.

The verdict remains SUPPORTED. The evidence confirms both that Meta's effective tax rate increased in 2025 (from 12% to 30% for the full year) and that this increase was mainly due to the $15.93 billion one-time charge related to OBBBA (U.S. tax law changes).
